intro: The trick is to start small. One agent, used properly for a week, beats five half-built ones. Here's a gentle month that fits around a full-time job.
saves: This pace means about 30–60 minutes a week of setup, and by the end of the month the agents are giving you back more time than they take.

weeks.title: Choose and launch one agent
tasks: Decide your platform using the comparison (module 07) and sign up with your business email.
Build your first agent from a template. 'Business in 15 minutes' or 'Enquiry first replies' are good starters.
Run the test prompt and check it against 'what good looks like'.
Use it on demand for the rest of the week.

weeks.title: Review and tweak
tasks: Read back what it produced. What did you change every time?
Add those changes to the instructions (edit the agent in My agents and re-copy).
If you're happy, switch it on to a schedule.
Jot down roughly how much time it saved.

weeks.title: Add a second agent
tasks: Pick a different part of the business, e.g. the weekly content and follow-ups planner.
Build it, test it and use it on demand first.
Keep reading everything the first agent produces, just a quicker skim now.

weeks.title: Settle in and decide
tasks: Review both agents: keep, tweak or switch off?
Check your platform costs against the time saved (the calculator in module 07).
Export a backup of My agents.
Choose your next idea from the gallery, or enjoy the evenings back.

day30: Day 30 check: Are you spending less time on busywork? Do you trust the drafts? Is anything going out that you haven't read? If it's yes, yes, no, you're doing it exactly right.

sections.heading: An agent is…
lines: An AI you give a goal, not just a question.
It plans, uses tools, checks, then hands back to you.

sections.heading: The six parts
lines: Instructions: the briefing
Tools: what it can use
Knowledge: your reference folder
Memory: what it remembers
Trigger: what starts it
Guardrails: your rules and approval

sections.heading: Traffic lights
lines: Green: just for me, so let it run
Amber: client or public, so it drafts and I send
Red: money, legal, health, complaints, earnings, so I do it

sections.heading: Always check
lines: Prices and availability: with the supplier
Visa and entry rules: on GOV.UK (FCDO)
Anything public: facts, offers, tone

sections.heading: Never
lines: Use NHS devices, accounts or NHS Copilot for the business
Paste passports, health or card details into AI
Make income claims or auto-send marketing

sections.heading: When it goes wrong
lines: Don't just fix the output; fix the instructions
Pause the schedule if you're unsure
Ask the AI: 'How do I…?'
